items.title: China Historical GIS, Version 6
items.who: Fairbank Center, Harvard, and Fudan University
items.note: Time-series administrative units across dynasties, usable for placing Song iron offices, sites and quotas on a map.

items.title: A Survey Study of the Blast Furnace at Kuangshan Village Using 3D Laser Scanning
items.who: J. Wang, X. Huang and W. Qian
items.note: Laser-scanned the standing Northern Song furnace at Kuangshan, Wu'an, the tallest surviving ancient Chinese blast furnace, to reconstruct its form and operation.

items.title: China, Europe, and the Great Divergence: A Study in Historical National Accounting, 980–1850
items.who: S. Broadberry, H. Guan and D. D. Li
items.note: Builds Chinese GDP estimates from 980, including Northern Song industrial output, giving a macroeconomic frame against which iron output claims can be checked.

items.title: Coal-fuelled crucible lead-silver smelting in 12th–13th century China: A technological innovation in the age of deforestation
items.who: S. Liu, T. Rehren, D. Qin, J. Chen and W. Zhou
items.note: Excavated evidence for coal-fuelled non-ferrous smelting, while arguing that most iron smelters of the period still used charcoal-fired furnaces.

items.title: The Making of Song Dynasty History: Sources and Narratives, 960–1279 CE
items.note: Traces how the Song state compilations behind the Song huiyao and Song shi were assembled, relevant to how far their fiscal figures can be trusted.

items.title: From Bloomery Iron to Cast Iron: Spatial Distribution Patterns and Influencing Factors of Ancient Iron Smelting Technology in Southeastern Guangxi, China
items.who: R. Liu, G. Zou, Y. Zhao et al.
items.note: GIS analysis of 38 Han to Song smelting sites in southeastern Guangxi, mapping bloomery and cast-iron production clusters and their geological controls.
